archive_05_001.speaker: narrator
archive_05_001.text: The road assessment arrived before the breakfast bowls were cleared. A maintenance crew had reopened the ridge bridge to light carts, excluding stacked timber and any crossing during heavy rain. The boundary clerk's village lay beyond it. The district registrar appointed a visiting records scribe to conduct the requested interview and inspect any offered source. He would travel as a paid courier and witness to his own case, not as sole custodian of the resulting packet. Dai assigned Yue to copying support within her current paid hours.

archive_05_002.speaker: narrator
archive_05_002.text: The board authorised forty-six copper from the two-hundred qualified-work allowance: eight for shared cart transport, twelve for He's courier work, ten for the visiting scribe's appointment, twelve for two nights of simple lodging and meals for three people, and four for the retired clerk's agreed interview time. The payment did not depend on testimony favouring the family. That left one hundred and fifty-four for later qualified tasks. Yue checked the rates with the actual travellers before Dai committed the money. A number could add correctly while describing rooms nobody had agreed to provide.

archive_05_003.speaker: narrator
archive_05_003.text: They would leave on the twenty-seventh day. Yue's twenty-eighth remained her scheduled rest day, spent at the village inn rather than converted into an interview because the witnesses happened to be nearby. The scribe agreed to conduct the formal work on the following morning. If He chose to carry an unrelated paid letter during the interval, it would be his task and his rest arrangement, not a claim on Yue. He looked amused by the explanation until she asked whether he would enjoy having someone sell the same day of his life twice.

archive_05_004.speaker: he_xi
archive_05_004.text: I have been trying to persuade my mother that waiting is not the only work I can do. You are trying to persuade this archive that staying nearby is not the same as accepting work. Perhaps we should trade arguments when either of us becomes tired of his own. I will deliver one small letter on the village road if it remains safe. After that I intend to eat whatever the inn calls supper and complain about it without writing a report. The complaint will be for pleasure.

archive_05_005.speaker: narrator
archive_05_005.text: The cart left with two ordinary parcels and the three travellers' packs. The scribe kept the registry instruction in a closed case, while He carried the outward receipt for the recovered instrument's certified extract. Yue carried blank copying paper and her ordinary notebook. The orchard trustees had received notice of the interview and appointed a contact to receive its permitted result. They had not sent an escort. Their absence did not make the district work a private conversation belonging only to He, and the scribe explained that before the road grew too noisy.

archive_05_006.speaker: narrator
archive_05_006.text: The first ascent followed a channel cut into rock. Autumn leaves lay over its edges, making deep places appear shallow. The driver stopped at each blind turn and called ahead. He offered to walk the narrow stretch, taking his own pack from the cart. Yue and the scribe did the same after the driver named the permitted load. Walking reduced the cart's burden but did not erase a weak bridge. At the crossing they waited while the maintenance watcher checked the water mark against the reopening conditions.

archive_05_007.speaker: narrator
archive_05_007.text: The watcher let them pass one cart at a time. From the bridge Yue could see old boards caught in the reeds downstream, remains of the previous damaged span. He pointed out the footpath he had used during the closure, climbing above the ravine and returning through a quarry. It had added most of a day to his route. The driver said he had lost two weeks of work entirely. Their descriptions made the reopened bridge feel less like an available line on a map and more like labour returned to many different people.

archive_05_008.speaker: narrator
archive_05_008.text: Above the ravine, the road broadened between dwarf pines. Yue could look away from her feet for several steps without risking a twisted ankle. He told her how his grandmother had taught him to identify a safe resting stone: not merely flat, but clear of the slope where loose stones fell. She had brought apples for him to eat there and claimed the uphill ones tasted sweeter. He knew now she had simply saved the unbruised fruit for the ascent. He said he preferred the explanation she invented.

archive_05_009.speaker: lin_yue
archive_05_009.text: An unbruised apple tastes different when someone has kept it for you. The story does not have to be literally true to carry that fact. I would write a different account if we were measuring orchard sales, but this is the part of the road where you are telling me about your grandmother. I hope we can let her keep the sweeter hill. It should not be required to certify a deed before it is allowed to remain a good memory.

archive_05_010.speaker: narrator
archive_05_010.text: The scribe, walking a little ahead, pretended not to hear the last exchange. He had warned them that the interview would separate memory from documents; he did not insist every roadside conversation use the same form. At the next rest stop he produced a hard sweet from his case and confessed his children accused him of counting even the clouds. He gave one sweet to each traveller and kept the broken piece. He objected when Yue remarked on the division, saying the broken piece dissolved sooner and therefore saved work.

archive_05_011.speaker: narrator
archive_05_011.text: The inn stood beside a terrace of cabbages held down with stones. Its owner showed them three sleeping places, a covered common table and a basin that had to be refilled from the yard well. The agreed twelve copper covered the three travellers for two nights with plain meals. Any extension would require a new price and approval. Yue checked that the loft ladder was sound before choosing the upper sleeping place. He chose the bed near the door because early courier customers tended to knock there whether invited or not.

archive_05_012.speaker: narrator
archive_05_012.text: The scribe sent an arrival note to the retired boundary clerk without calling for immediate work. The clerk replied through a grandson that morning tea would suit him on the twenty-ninth. He asked the visitors to bring the question list first, because his hearing was poor and surprise made it worse. The scribe delivered the written list that afternoon under the district procedure; Yue did not join because her copied questions were already complete. She watched a chicken steal a thread from the inn's drying cloth and carry it away like a legal victory.

archive_05_013.speaker: narrator
archive_05_013.text: Her rest day began with no bell and no request at the foot of the loft ladder. She lay still long enough to discover an ache in her shoulders that work had concealed. Outside, He was bargaining over the rate for his small letter. The requester wanted to call the route a favour because He was already going past. He replied that he was not going past until they agreed a route. Yue smiled into her folded coat and stayed where she was. A neighbouring room's cough reminded her that rest could be ordinary and still be fortunate.

archive_05_014.speaker: narrator
archive_05_014.text: Later she walked to the village's public well. The rest-day guidance allowed the short open path, and she left word at the inn about where she was going. An old woman filling a bucket asked whether the strangers had come to buy orchard land. Yue said she had come to help copy a district interview. The woman shrugged and warned her that ink dried slowly in this valley. It was advice without curiosity, given to a traveller who would soon discover it was useful. Yue bought no history in exchange for the bucket warning.

archive_05_015.speaker: narrator
archive_05_015.text: He returned before noon with his delivery receipt. He had passed a public post station and purchased a single sheet to write to his father. The letter was not part of the case packet. He sat over it so long that the inn owner placed lunch beside him without asking whether the words were ready. Yue took her bowl to the other end of the table. She could see him cross out an opening twice. When he finally wrote steadily, his expression grew more angry rather than less.

archive_05_016.speaker: narrator
archive_05_016.text: He asked whether she would read the opening as a friend, not as the archive's assistant. Yue agreed to the two sentences he offered. They told his father that the descendant clause had been found and that his mother had made the earlier archive journey alone. Neither sentence asked the father to defend himself. He wanted to add that leaving had been easier than fighting. Yue said she could not know whether that was true. He stared at the sentence until its certainty began to offend him more than the absence of an answer.

archive_05_017.speaker: he_xi
archive_05_017.text: I know why he left in the account my mother gives when she is tired. I know a different reason when she is trying to be fair. I know almost nothing he has said for himself. That does not excuse the years I carried things he could have carried. It makes the sentence harder to write. I can tell him the clause is found and ask whether he will speak to the registrar. I do not have to give him a completed life before he has answered the letter.

archive_05_018.speaker: narrator
archive_05_018.text: He posted the shorter letter and kept no copy for the case, because it asked a family question he had not offered as evidence. Yue spent the rest of the afternoon repairing her coat cuff with thread bought at the inn. Her stitches were ugly but strong enough. He tried to demonstrate a courier's quick strap knot and caught his thumb in it. They laughed until the scribe returned and asked which crucial professional technique had failed. He showed him the knot, and the scribe demonstrated an equally bad one from his years tying document cases.

archive_05_019.speaker: narrator
archive_05_019.text: The twenty-ninth morning was cold enough to make the well rope stiff. The retired clerk met them in a room facing east, with a square of sunlight placed almost exactly where his chair stood. He had the written questions open on a board and asked the scribe to speak toward his good ear. His grandson brought tea and left at the clerk's request. The room smelled of stored onions and clean wool. Yue set her paper on the permitted end of the table while He sat beside the door, not directly opposite the witness.

archive_05_020.speaker: narrator
archive_05_020.text: The clerk remembered the founder's orchard settlement because the survey had taken place during a failed apple harvest. He had inspected boundary stones and witnessed the land transfer to the orchard trust. He remembered an argument over the lower house and the school gate, but refused to supply its words until he had looked at his retained survey note. The note belonged to his own work records, whose deposit terms allowed relevant extracts for a district land inquiry. He offered the page after the scribe read that purpose back to him.

archive_05_021.speaker: narrator
archive_05_021.text: The survey drawing marked the orchard tract in dark ink. The lower house lay outside the shaded transfer area, though its adjoining drainage strip crossed the boundary. A margin stated that existing occupation rights remained under separate instruments. The date matched the cross-reference on the revision application. The scribe compared the note's record number to the registry instruction and wrote down the match. He began to smile, then saw the clerk frown at a second entry. The later drain amendment had enlarged one access strip. It did not say what happened to the house right.

archive_05_022.speaker: narrator
archive_05_022.text: The clerk explained that the founder had initially asked to replace several agreements with one orchard settlement. The registry had required separate treatment for existing occupation rights. The general transfer could proceed without ending the house tenancy. A later house revision would therefore need its own completed record and notices. He had witnessed the orchard boundaries, not any revocation of the descendants' clause. His memory was helpful because it led to a surviving note; the note itself supplied a narrower conclusion than the broad story He wanted to carry home.

archive_05_023.speaker: narrator
archive_05_023.text: The scribe asked whether the clerk knew why the house revision request remained cross-referenced to the orchard transfer. He did not. A clerk at the office might have attached the incomplete request to the completed survey for convenience, or a later paper could remain elsewhere. The retired man did not remember handling it. Yue wrote the uncertainty without asking him to search his feelings harder. Poor hearing had made him tired, and he began answering a previous question instead of the present one. The scribe stopped the interview for tea.

archive_05_024.speaker: narrator
archive_05_024.text: During the break, the clerk asked He whether the lower house still had a crooked plum tree. He said it did, though orchard children stole the fruit before it ripened. The old man laughed and remembered doing the same with other survey apprentices. The tree had been crooked even then. For a moment the table held no competing instrument at all. He described his grandmother threatening the thieves with a broom while leaving a bowl of bruised fruit beside the gate. The clerk listened with his face turned toward the good ear.

archive_05_025.speaker: narrator
archive_05_025.text: The interview resumed only for the specific missing fields. The clerk permitted the relevant survey extract and his bounded statement to go to the registrar and the notified parties. He declined wider publication of his old notebook, which included unrelated household boundaries. The four-copper time payment was handed over against its ordinary receipt. He asked whether he could keep it if the registry later found him mistaken. The scribe explained again that it paid for an honest interview, including uncertainty and correction. It was not a reward for an answer.

archive_05_026.speaker: narrator
archive_05_026.text: Yue read her copied extract aloud slowly. The clerk corrected one compass direction before signing; his pointing finger had followed the road bend rather than the written north mark. The drawing and corrected transcription stayed together. He was embarrassed by the slip until Yue showed him where she had almost copied the same direction from his first gesture. Two people could share a mistake without making it more authoritative. The scribe noted the correction and prepared the closed district packet, leaving the clerk's original notebook in his room.

archive_05_027.speaker: narrator
archive_05_027.text: Outside, He climbed three steps and sat down abruptly. Yue thought he was ill, but he put his hands over his face and began to laugh. The house had not been included in the orchard transfer. It was a good fact, though the separate revision still required a registry search. He had heard the limitations. He was laughing because a shaded corner on a modest survey drawing had refused to erase his grandmother's doorway. Yue waited until he could stand without turning the laughter into a speech about gratitude.

archive_05_028.speaker: lin_yue
archive_05_028.text: The report will say what the note supports. You can be pleased with that before the next inquiry arrives. I saw the marked boundary and heard the clerk distinguish what he witnessed from what he did not. The registry will check the separate house trail. None of that requires you to keep your face solemn today. We will still need to get the packet home dry. Perhaps save one laugh for the driver, who will want to know why three people suddenly like a survey drawing so much.

archive_05_029.speaker: narrator
archive_05_029.text: They returned to the inn intending to leave after the afternoon route assessment. The bridge watcher sent word first: rising water had reached the closure mark, and light carts would wait. A maintenance crew was checking the higher quarry path for walkers. The driver would not risk his cart on it. He inspected the route notice and said he could probably go on foot alone. The scribe declined to release the district packet into a probably. It remained in his closed case until a permitted transport route reopened or an authorised alternative was confirmed.

archive_05_030.speaker: narrator
archive_05_030.text: The inn owner's extension price was three copper per traveller for another night with meals, higher than the initial group quote because fresh grain delivery had been delayed. The scribe used the district message station to request authorisation from the archive's board contact. The contact approved one further night at nine copper from the qualified-work allowance. The remaining amount fell from one hundred and fifty-four to one hundred and forty-five. Yue wrote the changed return date for her current appointment, with no extra wage day created beyond the calendar days already running.

archive_05_031.speaker: narrator
archive_05_031.text: The maintenance notice allowed walkers over the quarry path after inspection, but named a steep section unsuitable for heavy carriers in rain. He wanted to go home with his own small pack and leave the packet with the scribe. Yue asked what he would gain by arriving before the report. He said his mother was waiting and he was tired of making her wait. The reason was real, but the mountain slope remained the same. He sent a short arrival-delay message through the public relay instead, paying its ordinary family-message fee from his own pouch.

archive_05_032.speaker: narrator
archive_05_032.text: Rain filled the terrace channels that night. The inn owner moved the cabbage stones, which had become small dams, and directed runoff away from the sleeping rooms. The three visitors helped carry a table after she checked the path and named the safe position. It took a few minutes within the lodging emergency arrangements. Nobody opened the records case to use paper as a wedge. Afterwards Yue washed mud from her hands and watched the window's reflected lamp tremble in the basin. She felt how easily a closed road made a traveller's body start bargaining with common sense.

archive_05_033.speaker: narrator
archive_05_033.text: The scribe told a story about his first registry appointment, when he had transported a parcel through a flood to prove he could be relied on. He reached the office safely and discovered the parcel held blank forms that another district had overstocked. His supervisor had praised him before opening it. He had kept the praise for years before admitting the route choice was foolish. He no longer decided a document's importance by the trouble already spent carrying it. He decided what its actual task justified before he stepped into the water.

archive_05_034.speaker: narrator
archive_05_034.text: He slept badly and came down before dawn. The inn owner had banked her fire under its normal night cover, leaving embers to revive for breakfast. He sat nearby with his family receipt between his fingers. Yue found him there while fetching water. He said the word waiting had begun to feel like an accusation no matter who spoke it. She said a clerk waiting for bridge inspection was doing something different from an institution forgetting a family inquiry. He nodded, not because the distinction made waiting pleasant, but because it let him stop blaming the water personally.

archive_05_035.speaker: narrator
archive_05_035.text: On the thirtieth morning, the bridge remained closed while the maintenance crew removed debris pressing against one pier. Their ordinary work was visible from the safe waiting point, and the driver explained why people could not hurry them by standing closer. The inn owner let the travellers stay through the afternoon without another lodging charge if they left before supper. The archive contact authorised a second night only if required. It would cost another nine and leave one hundred and thirty-six in the allowance. The scribe recorded the conditional approval without treating it as spent.

archive_05_036.speaker: narrator
archive_05_036.text: The crew reopened the crossing late in the day for one light cart under supervision. The driver chose to cross before dark and reach the lower receiving house rather than attempt the final mountain ascent at night. Its existing traveller accommodation could take the three visitors under their travel arrangement without another inn extension. They arrived with the case dry and the hired driver paid according to the agreed return fare. The conditional second night remained unspent. Yue kept both the approval and the note explaining that it had not been used.

archive_05_037.speaker: narrator
archive_05_037.text: The lower house clerk had received He's delay message for onward delivery. He had no reply yet. She pointed him toward supper rather than suggesting the absence meant his mother was angry. Yue took the upper sleeping mat and marked the thirtieth paid day in her notebook. The calendar had continued while their return route did not. She had six days left in the first appointment, and the renewal offer awaited her answer. Winter on the mountain now seemed less abstract after a bridge had held three people's plans beside a cabbage field.

archive_05_038.speaker: narrator
archive_05_038.text: They climbed to the archive on the thirty-first morning with the ordinary carter taking only the inspected load. The first winter supply cart had arrived in their absence. Tan reported twenty-four accepted fuel sacks and two hundred and forty accepted kitchen shares. Winter totals now stood at fifty-two sound sacks and five hundred and eighty shares, with the remaining deliveries still expected. The damp old sacks remained segregated pending the merchant's inspection. Goods on a road invoice had become counted stores only after the people at the mountain had examined them.

archive_05_039.speaker: narrator
archive_05_039.text: The replacement beam was installed, and the carpenter had completed the northern span's load inspection. The hall could reopen after the workroom dust cleaning and final handling clearances, not at the instant the carpentry invoice was signed. The roof account held its own receipts: the archive reserve and grant instalments paid only the approved materials, labour and transport. Dai gave the travellers these ordinary updates before asking for the boundary report. He smiled at the fuel total because it meant they had returned to a place whose other work had continued without him.

archive_05_040.speaker: narrator
archive_05_040.text: The scribe delivered the closed district interview packet under receipt. He's mother received the permitted party copy through her appointed case contact. Dai and Luo read the archive's authorised procedural summary, including the separate-house trail the registry still needed to check. The orchard representative received the same offered survey extract and witness statement under the clerk's scope. The notebook itself remained beyond the ridge with its owner. Yue put her working transcription beside the checked extract, marking it completed rather than keeping an informal duplicate among her personal road notes.

archive_05_041.speaker: narrator
archive_05_041.text: He saw his mother at the outer gate. She touched his shoulder first, then asked whether he had eaten on the return road. He said yes and showed her the authorised survey extract. They stood over the shaded boundary until she took his arm and led him toward the house where they currently rented rooms. Yue looked away. The recovered doorway could enter a family conversation without an archive assistant standing by to admire its meaning. Dai watched her look away and gave her the afternoon off from extra meetings, keeping her ordinary copying work within its planned hours.

archive_05_042.speaker: narrator
archive_05_042.text: Luo wanted to know whether the witness had sounded confident. The scribe answered that confidence was not the strongest feature of the interview. Its strongest feature was a retained survey note linked to the registry reference, with a witness who clearly separated his boundary work from a house revision he did not remember. Luo accepted that, though the answer gave him no triumphant public sentence. Dai attached the summary to the case movement list. The clerk's uncertain memory had produced a more reliable next inquiry than a sweeping recollection would have done.

archive_05_043.speaker: narrator
archive_05_043.text: The district registry requested its own older completion bundle the same day. Its staff expected to trace the separate house revision before deciding whether a formal hearing could take place prior to winter closure. The retired boundary clerk's signed statement could stand under the ordinary procedure without making him climb to the mountain immediately. A later challenge might require further questions, with his agreement and safe travel considered then. He had not promised to remain permanently available. Yue felt grateful that the procedure could protect a witness without asking him to become a prisoner of his useful afternoon.

archive_05_044.speaker: narrator
archive_05_044.text: In the kitchen, the cook counted the winter delivery's food shares again against the component sheets. She found a sack label smeared by rain but the weighed contents correct. The merchant's clerk supplied a replacement label under the same lot record rather than altering the accepted quantity. Tan used the report as a lesson for the store assistant: a damaged label and a short sack were different problems. Yue ate her meal while listening, relieved that an archive could speak about rice with the same care it brought to an inheritance clause.

archive_05_045.speaker: narrator
archive_05_045.text: Sun came for a borrowed jar and asked Yue how the road had behaved. Yue described the closed bridge and the inn's cabbages, leaving the private interview inside its authorised record. Sun said waiting among cabbages sounded preferable to waiting among officials. She had once spent a day in a district office whose stool pinched her leg, and remembered that stool more clearly than the document she obtained. Yue told her the cook wanted the borrowed jar washed. Sun replied that this was the first truly demanding official request she had heard all week.

archive_05_046.speaker: narrator
archive_05_046.text: That evening Yue examined the renewal terms Dai had prepared. The ninety-six calendar days would begin immediately after her first thirty-six, ending on the one-hundred-and-thirty-second day from arrival. Five copper per calendar day totalled four hundred and eighty, with weekly rest and meals under the winter kitchen plan. Duties remained copying, authorised supported movement and bounded inspected control tasks. Qualified roof, heater and preservation decisions belonged to their appointed workers. Yue read the weather-closure clause twice. A blocked departure would require continued lodging and a separately agreed arrangement after the term.

archive_05_047.speaker: narrator
archive_05_047.text: The clause reserved shelter during a road closure without calling every sheltered hour a work assignment. If the archive needed additional work after the appointment, it would offer an extension with dates and pay. If no safe route opened, Yue could remain sheltered while an actual departure plan was made, with kitchen consumption recorded. The board's hundred extra shares could help but did not become limitless insurance. She asked where responsibility would lie if those shares ran short. Dai named the board's emergency contact and the ordinary district supply procedure, including the possibility that no immediate delivery could reach them.

archive_05_048.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_05_048.text: I cannot sign a promise that the mountain will always let food through. I can sign who must make the next decision, which stores we have, what money remains and when we must ask for help. You have just seen a bridge close on a modest autumn journey. Winter will make some decisions slower. I would like you to stay because your work is useful and because you ask where a promise ends. I do not want that usefulness to hide a condition you would refuse if I spoke plainly.

archive_05_049.speaker: narrator
archive_05_049.text: Yue asked for the daily winter store reports to be available to resident staff, with household visitors' private particulars excluded. Dai agreed; the quantities belonged in the common planning notice. Luo added that the public readers should also see closure and reopening reasons without needing to ask a personal favour. They wrote these duties into their respective schedules. Yue did not sign yet. She had until the thirty-sixth day to answer, and wanted to use the remaining time as the actual decision interval offered to her. Dai put the unsigned page in its marked cover.

archive_05_050.speaker: narrator
archive_05_050.text: He received a reply from his father on the thirty-second day. He did not bring it to the archive case table. He took it to his mother first. Later he told Yue only that his father had agreed to answer the registrar's relevant questions and would come if a hearing date was safely reachable. The family letter remained theirs. He looked less satisfied than he had after the survey note, and considerably less certain what anger should do next. Yue asked whether he wanted to walk to the upper gate after her work ended.

archive_05_051.speaker: narrator
archive_05_051.text: They walked without the petition bundle. The repaired roof held a pale line of new slates against the old ones, and the yard had regained its ordinary route after the timber stack moved. He said his father had left because he could no longer earn enough locally after a hand injury. The work he found elsewhere paid badly at first. He had sent less money than he promised and then fewer letters because each needed another explanation. He had still left things undone. Knowing why had not given He a childhood with a different father.

archive_05_052.speaker: he_xi
archive_05_052.text: When I wrote the letter I wanted an answer that would tell me whether to keep being angry. He has given me facts, and I can be angry beside them. My mother says that is what she has been doing for years. I used to think she was indecisive. Perhaps she had already reached a place I am just beginning to see. I will let the registrar ask about the path work. I will ask about the rest when we can speak without a clerk making columns between us.

archive_05_053.speaker: narrator
archive_05_053.text: The second supply cart arrived that afternoon with another twenty-four accepted fuel sacks and two hundred and forty shares. Winter stock rose to seventy-six sound sacks and eight hundred and twenty daily shares. The final order would add twenty sacks and two hundred and forty shares if accepted as contracted. The cook checked the store doors and refused a volunteer's offer to leave food parcels anonymously in the winter cupboard. Gifts could be welcomed after inspection and entry; anonymous abundance would confuse a count that people might later trust with their lives.

archive_05_054.speaker: narrator
archive_05_054.text: The carpenter returned for the hall's final reopening inspection after cleaning. Tan had checked the cleared packet routes, and Dai had returned the moved public references to their revised shelves under count. The locked deposits remained in their authorised supports. Luo posted the next reading session and its market-day equivalent. Nothing in the room appeared splendid. New timber, clean walking space and fewer buckets made a restrained improvement. Yue stood at the doorway and found that restraint beautiful, perhaps because she had now seen how much agreement it required.

archive_05_055.speaker: narrator
archive_05_055.text: The first returning reader brought a receipt for a certified copy issued years earlier. He wanted a fresh extract after the older sheet had torn at its fold. The clerk compared the receipt, identified the public source and offered the ordinary replacement fee with the announced subsidy procedure if needed. The man paid without asking for help, then waited while the checked copy was prepared. Luo watched from the desk without counting him twice for having returned. Winter access had begun as an ordinary transaction rather than the cheerful crowd his grant letter once imagined.

archive_05_056.speaker: narrator
archive_05_056.text: The roof account closed at nine hundred and eighty copper. The council's seven hundred and twenty and the archive's two hundred and sixty had covered the specified work, including the supplier's rejected-beam replacement at no extra charge to the archive under the agreed terms. Dai filed the final inspection and receipts together, leaving the hall's continuing checks on the ordinary maintenance schedule. A closed project account did not declare the mountain permanently dry. It meant one named repair had been delivered and paid for, giving later workers a clear place to begin.

archive_05_057.speaker: narrator
archive_05_057.text: Yue spent the thirty-third morning comparing old movement entries under the independent review. The house paper's recovery had prompted a wider check, but the ten-entry scope kept the task finishable. Two entries lacked destination details; both objects were found safely after an ordinary shelf comparison. Their owners did not lose private access terms because the catalogue needed correction. The visiting council clerk signed the procedural findings. Dai read the summary aloud at the staff meeting, naming her approval failures and Luo's handling failure without turning either person into the sole explanation for years of institutional habit.

archive_05_058.speaker: narrator
archive_05_058.text: Luo proposed placing retrieval follow-ups in a shared queue rather than keeping them among his own desk drafts. Dai agreed to a list visible to the authorised staff, with private contents represented only by case number and action date. The system would not discover every lost note. It would make unfinished work less dependent on the memory of one helpful steward. Yue helped move the current entries, including the house revision query. The act resembled copying until she saw Luo set down the bundle he had carried from desk to desk for years.

archive_05_059.speaker: narrator
archive_05_059.text: The district registrar sent word that the house revision bundle had been located and required comparison with a register endorsement in another volume. A proposed hearing could be held at the lower receiving house before the first deep snow if the endorsement arrived in time. All notified parties would receive the date together. The registry did not yet declare the descendant condition active or void. He accepted the update without demanding the archive convert proposed into certain. His mother asked about travel arrangements, and the clerk gave the known options without promising a carriage through weather.

archive_05_060.speaker: narrator
archive_05_060.text: The final winter delivery was delayed below by a wheel repair. Its goods stayed outside the mountain stock: seventy-six accepted fuel sacks and eight hundred and twenty shares remained the truthful count. The merchant sent the delay notice and a new expected arrival on the thirty-fifth day, still within the contracted delivery window. Tan inspected the winter store's ventilation while waiting. The cook adjusted no meals from those sealed supplies. The incompleteness was visible on the common notice, where people could see exactly what the mountain did and did not yet hold.

archive_05_061.speaker: narrator
archive_05_061.text: That night Yue laid the unsigned renewal beside her ordinary pack. Leaving after thirty-six days would fulfil her first agreement. Staying would mean winter work, a closed road at times and people whose questions no longer seemed merely assigned. She thought of the inn's slow bridge notice, Sun's refusal to become a general memory, He's letter and the supported house paper. None commanded her to remain. They had shown her the shape of work she could choose with enough knowledge to own the choice. She slept before deciding.

archive_05_062.speaker: narrator
archive_05_062.text: On her thirty-fifth day's scheduled rest, she chose to sign the appointment after reading its dates and provisions once more. Dai signed for the archive, and Luo witnessed the acceptance without praising it as sacrifice. The reserved four hundred and eighty became committed wages for the term beginning on day thirty-seven. Weekly rest carried forward on the existing seven-day cycle. Yue kept her own copy, stored with the old appointment rather than among case papers. Her winter staying belonged to her employment, not to the house claimant's need for a favourable ending.

archive_05_063.speaker: narrator
archive_05_063.text: The final supply cart reached the yard on the thirty-fifth afternoon. Twenty sound fuel sacks and two hundred and forty food shares passed inspection, bringing the winter reserves to ninety-six sacks and one thousand and sixty shares. The clerk closed the six-hundred supply commitment against all three delivery receipts. The three damp old sacks remained a separate supplier-return matter and added nothing to the accepted total. The board marked the winter programme's store opening for day thirty-seven, when Yue's new term would begin and the common consumption sheet would start.

archive_05_064.speaker: narrator
archive_05_064.text: The clerk paid the completed first appointment on its thirty-sixth day: one hundred and eighty copper for thirty-six calendar days at five each. Yue counted the coins and signed the wage receipt after comparing the dates, including the road wait and weekly rest. Her original eight-copper return fare remained reserved under the first agreement, to be carried forward for her eventual paid departure. She put the earned wages in her own pouch. The winter wage commitment would begin tomorrow, with its separate four-hundred-and-eighty total.

archive_05_065.speaker: narrator
archive_05_065.text: On the last evening of the first appointment, the cook served apples from the orchard worker's own small gift. He had offered them through the inspection and gift-entry procedure rather than letting the house dispute prevent an ordinary neighbourly act. He Xi ate one and said nothing about ownership. Dai set the next week's public hours beside the kitchen door. Luo made a new blue-sheep joke that nobody needed explained. Yue folded the completed thirty-six-day page into her notebook. Beyond the roof, the ridge darkened toward a winter they had finally supplied in quantities.
